brand_dna.category: Specialty coffee roaster selling small-batch blends and single origins, often tied to pro athlete and cause-driven collaborations.
brand_dna.core_belief: Coffee is a way to connect people and give back - blends are built with partners and benefit causes like Kingdom Home.
proof_points: Athlete collaboration blends (Gold Glove Blend with Ian Happ, Hope Blend with Matthew Boyd) plus the Morale Supply Co. partnership
Cause tie-ins: Hope Blend benefits Kingdom Home
Single-origin offerings such as Dominican Ramirez
brand_dna.positioning: Accessible, story-first specialty coffee (blends $16-$20) built on real partnerships rather than a purely premium or commodity play.

voice_pillars.name: Partnership-Driven
voice_pillars.desc: They lead with named collaborators, putting real people and teams at the center of each blend.
voice_pillars.quote: Gold Glove Blend // Connect Roasters with Ian Happ

voice_pillars.name: Cause-Minded
voice_pillars.desc: They frame products around giving back and supporting a specific mission.
voice_pillars.quote: Hope Blend x Matthew Boyd | Benefiting Kingdom Home

voice_pillars.name: Straight-Talking
voice_pillars.desc: They speak plainly and directly to shoppers, even flagging the fine print out loud.

icp: Sports fans and cause-conscious coffee drinkers who buy blends tied to athletes and charities they care about, valuing the story and mission as much as the cup.

personas.name: The Team Loyalist
personas.description: A baseball and sports fan who buys athlete-collab blends like Gold Glove or Morale to support players they follow.

personas.name: The Give-Back Buyer
personas.description: A values-driven shopper moved by cause tie-ins like Hope Blend benefiting Kingdom Home.

personas.name: The Everyday Explorer
personas.description: A curious coffee drinker who wants approachable blends and single origins like Dominican Ramirez without a premium price tag.
